basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Dixitque Adam: Mulier quam dedisti mihi sociam, dedit mihi de ligno et comedi. « Superbia'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Dixitque Adam: Mulier quam dedisti mihi sociam, dedit mihi de ligno et comedi. « Superbia nunquid dixit, peccavi? Habet deformitatem confusionis, et non habet humilitatem confessionis. Ad hoc ista conscripta sunt, quia et ipsae interrogationes nimirum ad hoc factae sunt, ut utiliter scriberentur, ut advertamus quomodo superbia laborent homines hodie, non nisi in Creatorem conantes referre si quid egerint mali, cum sibi velint tribui si quid egerint boni. Mulier, inquit, quam dedisti mihi sociam, dedit mihi de ligno et comedi, quasi ad hoc data sit, ut non ipsa potius obediret viro, et ambo Deo.
